repository.description: A multi-platform library for OpenGL, OpenGL ES, Vulkan, window and input

issue.body:
When the window is resizing the main thread of the application is frozen due to polling and event processing. In other 3D applications and games, the program should continue to run as the window is being resized and graphics content should continue to render as well.

This is likely the cause of: #443
I imagine that these issues are related because the AppKit API is likely trying to send an event to something that is locked up.

body: If those really are stack frame indices then it's likely that the workaround cited above causes a recursion loop.

Nope, not a recursion loop. I placed a printf in that method and didn't get any output right before it crashed.
Also the stack trace isn't exploding with recursion calls.

Left Side: x86 Code of the Crash
Right Side: [NSApplication SendEvent:]; implementation.

Ultimately it appears that GLFW is writing into a memory location in the VM that it no longer has access to. However I don't understand why NSZombie's won't catch it.

issue.body:
*After doing research I found that Apple puts an NSWindow to sleep using (AppNap) after the window reaches below 4 pixels in height.
*GLFW will now set a minimum height with the OS X default title bar height taken into consideration; this resolves the issue.

Closes: #443
